question: Why should Arjuna rise and fight if the enemies are already slain?
premises: Arjuna is told to rise and gain glory
He should conquer enemies and enjoy prosperous rule
The enemies are already slain by the Lord; Arjuna is mere instrument
inference: Arjuna acts as instrument while the Lord accomplishes the destruction
uncertainties: Fused sandhi forms are kept whole
plain_english: Therefore rise, gain glory; having conquered enemies, enjoy prosperous rule. These have already been slain by me; be a mere instrument, left-handed archer.
